summary: The notice and the days after: The notice is served, and someone in the household asks what happens by the date on it.
realLife: One life: A single mother of two in Houston who lost a fast-food job in March, fell two months behind on rent, and was denied unemployment benefits. A taunting notice on her door demanded her keys by evening. A legal aid lawyer said it carried no legal force, and the property company later said no eviction was filed and its manager was disciplined. Another: Furloughed in 2020 while in treatment for a second cancer, she got a notice and fought it, but was evicted in the fall. The family spent about six months in hotels, lost money to a rental scam, and she joined a tenant group and became its board president. Another: A single mother in Phoenix whose family caught COVID. She missed weeks of work, fell behind, and was evicted days before a federal moratorium ended. The family spent eighty days in hotels and short rentals paid by a fundraiser. Rental agencies refused her until a legal women's group helped her get rental aid. Another: A sheriff taped a notice to her door on a Friday evening the week before Christmas, giving her until Monday to leave a mobile home she owned on rented land. She owed under about $1,200 in lot rent and the owner would not take part payments. Her father negotiated away the debt, but the company kept the home.
